text: MCP's official quickstart builds a small weather server with two tools, get_alerts and get_forecast. The setup is deliberately minimal -- install the SDK, then decorate a function with @mcp.tool() to register it.

The SDK reads the function's type hints and its docstring to automatically generate the tool's inputSchema and description -- the exact JSON Schema shape from Lesson 14, built from code you were already going to write. You still own the quality of that docstring; a vague one-liner produces a vague tool description.

There's one real, specific failure mode worth knowing before you hit it: a stdio server must never write to stdout. The stdio transport uses standard input and output as the actual message channel, so a stray print() corrupts the JSON-RPC messages the client is parsing. Use the logging module instead -- it writes to stderr by default.
That rule is specific to stdio -- an HTTP-based server has no such problem, because its logs and its protocol messages don't share a channel.

Before writing code, scope the server the way Lesson 6 asked you to scope a tool schema: find the smallest useful set, give each tool one clear job with a docstring specific enough to pick from tools/list without guessing, and ask whether something is really a tool or would be a better fit as a read-only resource. Next: actually connecting an agent to a server like this.
